description: Successor amendment of the approved package v4.1 (Indy Init v4.1: Final Execution Optimization and Readiness Amendment). It changes no requirement, obligation, test binding, state machine or contract text. It moves the T10 bootstrap into the timed window at T0, its 29 minutes partly measured (2 measured, 27 estimated), classifies the F# contracts as specifications, removes the organizer-permission gate from the execution plan, gives the shared web entrypoints to integration with a change-request protocol, adds schedule sensitivity, and specifies the Praxis token-economics report. v4.1 itself is not edited: it stays as approved (APR-V41-OWNER-4).

changes.summary: T10 (bootstrap) runs at T0, inside the timed window, owned by integration, with a duration of 29 minutes, 2 of them measured on fresh empty repositories and 27 estimated (analysis/bootstrap-measurement.json). T11, T12, T14 and T18, the timed tasks without another timed predecessor, all follow it. Conditor's init runs first on the empty repository and the v4.1 generator layers onto it.

The F# contracts stay in the package as specifications. contract-classification.json classifies every contract file. X17 requires every contract to equal the reviewed v4.1 contract byte for byte (the guarantee), pins each allowed boundary member (the Credential and Confirmation code) by SHA-256, and runs a heuristic line scan for other code.

No task waits on organizer permission: T10's preference after T06 (organizer confirmation) is dropped, and AGENT-RULES no longer makes the bootstrap rely on ODR-V41-06. The published rules stay external constraints (STARTING-STATE.md), the historical records stay unchanged, and the residual interpretation risk is stated. The organizer-approval obligations of the frozen baseline (ADRP-016-O2, STORAGE-008-O1) and PRE-ORG-01/T06 stay unchanged; how they are reported is the owner's decision ODR-V411-02 (X19 scans v4's preflight checks, tasks, obligations and risk register, the waivers, and the listed documents for organizer gates, a heuristic over those sources, and requires a disposition for each it finds).

The token-economics report is produced from Praxis 3.24.0's own telemetry records by requirements-compiler token-economics (docs/TOKEN-ECONOMICS.md), verified with a recorded fixture in the offline suite.

web/index.html and web/causa.css are integration's (they were ui's). UI roles change them only through an integration-owned change request (X18 (the manifest; and AGENT-RULES may name the entrypoints only in reviewed lines pinned by SHA-256)); the ownership manifest and AGENT-RULES agree. Applying the UI change requests costs integration time: T17 carries 5 more minutes for T16's entrypoint requests; later requests fall in RES-INTEGRATION.

The schedule is recomputed with T10 at T0, with sensitivity scenarios for bootstrap and integration overruns. The reserves (RES-INTEGRATION 20, RES-FINAL 45) are unchanged and no estimate is shortened.

changeRequests.protocol: A UI role that needs a change to a shared entrypoint does not edit it. It opens a change request naming the file, the change (the exact markup or Forma-token rule) and the task it serves; integration applies it in its own pull request, in order, and the requesting role reviews that pull request. UI roles own their view modules (src/Causa.App/Views/*) and component-level presentation; the entrypoints only load them.
changeRequests.record: a Praxis work item owned by integration whose title starts with CR- and names the file, linked to the requesting task's work item
changeRequests.ruleSentence: It changes `web/index.html` and `web/causa.css` only through a change request to integration

startingState.residualRisk: The published rules say the repository starts empty and code starts at kickoff. They do not say whether material prepared before kickoff in executable form counts as planning or as code. Four kinds of material are at issue: the F# contract declarations, the deterministic generator, the layout assertions, and what conditor init writes at T0. conditor init writes the Echelon scaffold and imports 68 requirement documents (42 from this planning repository at commit 2eee2d5, 26 from Percepta). HACKATHON-BOUNDARIES lists, as an open question, whether a separate planning repository may be consumed directly by the blank implementation repository. The plan's boundary is that nothing is written to the competition repository before T0, and that everything written at T0 comes from approved, published sources. An organizer could read the materialized contract declarations, the Conditor scaffold, the requirements import, or the bootstrap itself as material prepared before kickoff. The plan does not claim otherwise. Whether organizer approval of the prepared material (ADRP-016-O2) is sought, and how it and R0.1-O1 are reported, is the owner's decision ODR-V411-02; the package as proposed does not seek it. If an organizer rules on the day, the team follows the ruling.
